s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of progressive shortness of breath and chest pain with associated hypertension and tachycardia
salient_findings: Progressive shortness of breath for one day duration
Chest tightness and non-radiating retrosternal chest pain
Bilateral coarse breathing sounds upon auscultation
key_facts: 80-year-old woman with history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia
Presented to emergency department with progressive shortness of breath
Accompanied by chest tightness and non-radiating retrosternal chest pain
Initial vital signs showed blood pressure of 191/99 mmHg
Heart rate of 114 beats per minute
Respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute
Oxygen saturation of 68% under ambient air
Patient was slightly drowsy but conversant and oriented
Bilateral coarse breathing sounds upon auscultation
Normal heart sounds without obvious murmurs or pericardial rubs
Serial Troponin-T measurements showed progressive elevation
Chest Radiography showed bilateral fine reticular opacities and cardiomegaly
EKG showed sinus tachycardia with mildly elevated ST-segments at the inferior leads

shortlist.label: Myocardial Infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive elevation of Troponin-T measurements and chest pain

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of shortness of breath and chest pain with associated tachycardia

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Edema
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral fine reticular opacities on chest X-ray and cardiomegaly

shortlist.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain and elevated ST-segments on EKG

shortlist.label: Lymphangitic Carcinomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral coarse breathing sounds and right anterior mediastinal mass on CT Angiography

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging studies, including bilateral fine reticular opacities on chest radiography and a mediastinal mass on CT angiography, along with the biopsy results showing epithelial malignancy of thymic origin, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myocardial Infarction
rejected.why: Although the patient has elevated troponin levels and chest pain, the coronary angiography shows diffusely slow coronary flow but patency in all three coronary arteries, and the echocardiography does not show regional wall motion abnormalities, making this less likely.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Embolism
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of pulmonary embolism on the imaging studies provided, and the patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Edema
rejected.why: While the patient has bilateral coarse breathing sounds and low oxygen saturation, the chest radiography shows bilateral fine reticular opacities but the echocardiography shows normal left ventricular contractility, which does not strongly support pulmonary edema as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's presentation with chest pain and elevated troponin levels could suggest acute coronary syndrome, but the coronary angiography results and the presence of a mediastinal mass with biopsy-proven malignancy point towards a different primary diagnosis.
